alerts.title: Progressive creatinine rise and proteinuria on TDF with regular NSAID use
alerts.message: Guidelines state that in patients on TDF, creatinine (eGFR) should be monitored and checked promptly during intercurrent illness or dehydration, as deterioration in renal function may occur. Patient shows a steady creatinine rise from 0.9 (2020) to 1.4 mg/dL (2026), eGFR now 52 mL/min/1.73m2, urinary protein 1+ and trace glucose, with no pre-visit renal review documented. TDF nephrotoxicity is a plausible contributor. Regular ibuprofen (2-3 times weekly for 6 months) is a further renal risk factor not addressed in the plan. Non-drug causes (hypertension is absent at BP 118/76, diabetes not reported, but proteinuria and glucosuria warrant evaluation) should also be considered.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat renal function and urinalysis promptly, assess eGFR trend, counsel to stop ibuprofen, and review TDF suitability per guideline renal monitoring. Consider switching tenofovir if renal decline is confirmed.

alerts.title: Viral load monitoring on DTG-based ART
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend viral load checks every 6 months on DTG-based first-line ART, with reduction to 12-monthly only if VL <50 copies/mL for over 1 year with reliable adherence. Patient has VL <50 copies/mL and adherence >95%, so routine 6-monthly review is appropriate, though no VL order is documented today.

evidence.recommended_action: Confirm viral load is scheduled per the 6-monthly DTG monitoring schedule and document the order.
